issue.body:
RUF105 in particular was being bad, because it would change our `noqa` to `ruff:ignore`, which then `black` looks at and reformats, which ruff would see being on the wrong line and remove + apply fixes arbitrarily around the codebase. Basically a giant mess.

I've disabled it. I wish we could get the nice human readable names (RUF106) without using `ruff:ignore`, but that doesn't seem possible.

issue.title: Treat Ruff ignore comments as pragmas
issue.body:
## Summary

- recognize canonical `# ruff:ignore[...]` comments as Black pragmas
- preserve original physical lines for Ruff ignores, matching `type: ignore`
- add direct and end-to-end regressions for #5260

Fixes #5260, closes #5266

## Testing

- `pytest tests/test_trans.py tests/test_format.py -k ruff`
- `pre-commit run -a`
- `env -u NO_COLOR tox -e py` — 476 passed, 1 skipped; 73 Jupyter tests passed

## AI-assisted contribution

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and review. I reviewed the final diff and verified all reported commands locally.

## Checklist

- [x] The change includes regression coverage.
- [x] Add the PR-numbered entry to `CHANGES.md`.

body: See also #3569 and #3946. I'm a bit wary of privileging comments understood by particular third-party tools.

I think the downsides of treating all `# xxx: yyy` comments as special are likely to be fairly small, and would save a lot of small pain. There are going to be cases where that will no longer fix normal comments that happen to have a colon in them, and distinguishing those cases might be more trouble than it's worth, but I think the net effect is positive.

I personally also like the suggestion of #3569 of having this configurable.


Trying to enumerate common tools would of course work as well, but would be a pain to maintain.

issue.title: Preserve ruff ignore pragmas when splitting lines
issue.body:
### Description

Fixes #5260.

Ruff's line-scoped `ruff:ignore` pragmas could be moved onto a nested expression when Black split an overlong line, changing which diagnostic the pragma suppresses. This change recognizes Ruff directives as pragmas and treats `ruff:ignore` comments like `type: ignore` comments when deciding whether a physical line can be split.

Both `# ruff:ignore[...]` and `# ruff: ignore[...]` forms are covered by regression tests.

Validation:

- `pytest tests/test_format.py -q` (232 passed)
- pre-commit on changed files: isort, flake8, mypy, EOF, trailing whitespace passed
- `git diff --check`

AI assistance was used during implementation. I independently reproduced the formatting change, reviewed the final diff, and ran the validation above.

### Checklist - did you ...

- [x] Implement any code style changes under the `--preview` style, following the stability policy? (No style change.)
- [x] Add an entry in `CHANGES.md` if necessary?
- [x] Add / update tests if necessary?
- [x] Add new / update outdated documentation? (No documentation change is needed.)

body:
> I think the downsides of treating all `# xxx: yyy` comments as special are likely to be fairly small, and would save a lot of small pain.

https://github.com/search?q=%2F%5B%5E%5Cs%5D+%2B%23+%5Cw%2B%3A+*%5B%5E%5Cn%5D%2F+language%3Apython&type=code

I feel like there's too many non-pragma comments here for that to be a good idea

Just a few heuristics makes the first few seem more reasonable:
 - the part before `:` must be lowercase ascii letters
 - after the `:` cannot be a `/` (just for links)

(I can't figure out how to make that search case-sensitive so I just ignored those)

https://github.com/search?q=%2F%28%3F-i%29%5B%5E%5Cs%23%5D%5B%5Ct+%5D*%23%5Cs*%5Ba-z%5D%2B%3A+*%5Ba-zA-Z%5D%2F+language%3Apython&type=code
Still a fair bit of false-positives. Examples include:
- `# default: foo`
- `# returns: foo` 
- `# units: m/s`
- `# example: foo`
- `# note: foo`

While these comments still apply directly to the line they're on, they're for humans and not for tooling, so it doesn't matter if the line is split or not.


Also worth highlighting is `# pragma: no-cover`. I'm not super familiar with Coverage.py, but my understanding is that these must be on the same line as the colon opening the block (or on the following line, but that's irrelevant here). So either of these work:
```py
if True:  # pragma: no-cover
if (
    True
):  # pragma: no-cover
```
If they are captured by our heuristic, they will be unnecessarily prevented from splitting, and we don't want to special-case certain tools.


P.S., if we do adopt a heuristic such like this, we can stop explicitly checking for `pylint` comments, but `noqa` needs to stay special-cased, since it can omit the `:` section, as well as often being uppercased. We could also probably stop explicitly checking `type` comments, but it might make sense to still, since they can be part of the AST, and we already special-case them to reformat them.

issue.title: Treat ruff:ignore as a pragma comment
issue.body:
### Problem

Lines annotated with `# ruff:ignore[...]` or `# ruff: ignore[...]` were reformatted by Black even though those pragmas must stay on the same line as the code they suppress:

```python
# Before formatting — this is already correct and should not change:
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx = 5  # ruff:ignore[bweh]

# After `black file.py` — incorrectly split:
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx = (
    5  # ruff: ignore[bweh]
)
```

`# type: ignore`, `# noqa`, and `# pylint:` are treated as pragma comments that prevent line splitting, but `# ruff:` was not included.

This is becoming more common: Ruff has a preview rule (`RUF101`) that converts all `# noqa` comments to `# ruff: ignore`, so the affected population will grow.

### Fix

Add `"# ruff:"` to the `startswith` check in `contains_pragma_comment` in `src/black/comments.py`. This covers both `# ruff:ignore[...]` and `# ruff: ignore[...]` (with or without a space after the colon).

### Testing

```python
# example.py
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx = 5  # ruff:ignore[bweh]
```

```bash
black --check example.py
# All done! ✨ 🍰 ✨
# 1 file would be left unchanged.
```

Fixes #5260

issue.title: Keep inline comments with the string when wrapping it in parentheses (#3802)
issue.body:
Closes #3802

When `StringParenWrapper` wraps a return/assign/assert value in parentheses so
the string can go on its own line, it moved any inline comment that followed the
string up to the opening-paren line. That silently changed which expression a
suppression comment applied to, so `# pyright: ignore[...]` (and similar) stopped
working — and there was no place the comment could be written that survived
formatting.

The comment now stays on the same line as the string it was written after.
Comments after a trailing comma or a pre-existing `(` are still moved up, as
before.

This changes the expected output of three existing unstable-style cases, updated
here: `preview_comments7`, `preview_long_strings` and
`preview_long_strings__regression`. A regression case for this issue is added as
`preview_comment_after_wrapped_string`.

Verified on this base: `tests/test_format.py` + `tests/test_black.py` go from 3
failures to 403 passed, with no newly failing test; re-running Black on the
formatted output is idempotent.

This patch was produced with the help of an autonomous coding system I build and
supervise. I review and test every change before submitting and follow up on
review feedback personally. If automated contributions are unwelcome in this
project, please say so and I will stop submitting them.

issue.title: Treat 'ruff: ignore' comments as unsplittable pragmas
issue.body:
## Summary

Black was reformatting lines that end with a `# ruff: ignore[code]` comment, even though those lines are exempt from ruff linting. Splitting such a line moves the pragma onto a different subexpression, silently breaking the suppression — the same reason Black never splits a line ending in `type: ignore`.

Changes:

- `src/black/nodes.py`: added `is_ruff_ignore_comment_string`, mirroring `is_type_ignore_comment_string`. It accepts both `ruff: ignore` and the spacing-free `ruff:ignore` form, with or without a bracketed rule list.
- `src/black/lines.py`: `Line.contains_unsplittable_type_ignore` now also treats a trailing `ruff: ignore` comment as unsplittable, so the RHS-splitting and other line-splitting paths leave these lines intact.
- `src/black/comments.py`: `contains_pragma_comment` recognizes `# ruff:` comments (for example `# ruff: noqa`) as pragmas, so string merging/splitting also leaves them alone.

## Tests

Added `tests/data/cases/ruff_ignore_pragma.py` covering both the spaced and spacing-free `ruff: ignore` forms on a line that previously got parenthesized.

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/test_format.py tests/test_black.py -q   # 403 passed, 8 subtests passed
python -m black --check src/black/lines.py src/black/nodes.py src/black/comments.py   # clean
python -m mypy src/black/lines.py src/black/nodes.py src/black/comments.py            # clean
```

Fixes #5260.

issue.title: Treat ruff directives as pragma comments (#5260)
issue.body:
Fixes #5260.

## What
A trailing `# ruff: ignore[...]` comment no longer prevents line splitting/merging. A 65-char name plus `= 5  # ruff: ignore[bweh]` (89 cols) was split into parens form, while the identical line with `# type: ignore[bweh]` stayed intact. Ruff directives are line-based: splitting the line can change which expression the directive applies to — the same corruption class as `# type: ignore`, which Black already protects.

## Scope decision (re the thread discussion)
@cobaltt7 and @A5rocks rightly flagged false positives in blanket-matching every `# word:` comment (`# default:`, `# note:`, `# units:` are human prose). This PR does **not** do that: it matches only the `# ruff:` prefix (ruff directives are always tooling, never prose), alongside the existing `# type:` / `# noqa` / `# pylint:` prefixes. Verified: a `# note: plain human comment` line on the same test case still splits as before.

## Changes
- `src/black/comments.py`: `contains_pragma_comment` also recognizes `# ruff:` (covers string-merge guards in `trans.py` via the shared helper).
- `src/black/nodes.py`: new `is_ruff_comment` / `is_ruff_comment_string` helpers (signature parity with `is_type_ignore_comment`).
- `src/black/lines.py`: `contains_unsplittable_type_ignore` also returns True for ruff directives on the last leaves.
- `tests/data/cases/ruff_pragma.py`: new data-driven case (ruff stays, type-ignore stays, human comment splits).
- `CHANGES.md`: entry under Unreleased → Stable style.

## Stable vs preview
Submitted as a stable correctness fix (it prevents directive corruption, same as type-ignore handling), not a style preference. Happy to gate behind preview if maintainers prefer — the change is isolated to the three call sites above.

## Evidence
- Repro before: 89-col ruff line split into parens; after: left unchanged (`1 file would be left unchanged`).
- New case: `test_simple_format[ruff_pragma.py]` passes.
- Related suites: 51 passed (`-k "ignore or pragma or fmtskip or comments"`).
- `black --check` on the three touched source files: clean.
